_readme: Words that carry clinical meaning, in Roman Urdu or English.
PURPOSE. Used by has_medical_signal() to answer one question: does this
text describe a complaint at all? A record containing none of these is a
fragment, and asking a language model to translate a fragment makes it
invent - 'band ho rha ha' ('is closing') came back as 'Arm is swollen'.
THIS FILE IS DATA, NOT CODE. Add a word by editing the right list below
and saving. No Python changes, no rebuild. tests/audit_pipeline.py
re-measures the whole list against the training corpus, so a bad edit is
caught rather than discovered by a user.
WHY A CURATED LIST AND NOT SOMETHING CLEVERER. Three alternatives were
built and measured on 2026-09-02, and all three were worse:
- vocabulary derived from the training corpus: the corpus is
cardiac-only and synthetic (276 distinct words), so it contains no
'bukhar' and no 'chot' at all, and rejected real complaints.
- asking the model to cite the source words it translated: destroyed
translation quality - 'sar mein chot lagi hai' (head injury) became
'There is a pain in my stomach'.
- a separate yes/no classifier call to the same model: 6/10, and the
failures were real complaints - 'bukhar', 'chakkar', 'saans phool
rahi hai' all classified as NOT a complaint.
The curated list scores 0 false rejections on 10,000 real complaints.
FAILURE DIRECTION IS DELIBERATE. A word missing from this file causes a
REFUSAL, never a wrong triage level. The clinician reads that complaint
themselves. That is the safe direction for this system: an unscored
patient is an inconvenience, an invented symptom is a hazard.
